questions.stem: In a quadrilateral $ABCD$, you know diagonal $AC = 15\text{ cm}$, $\angle BAC = 40°$, $\angle ACD = 55°$, $AB = 10\text{ cm}$, and $CD = 8\text{ cm}$. To find the area of the quadrilateral, which approach is best?

options.text: Split it into two triangles along diagonal $AC$ and use $\frac{1}{2}ab\sin C$ for each
Use the cosine rule on the whole quadrilateral
Multiply $AC$ by the average of the other sides
Use Pythagoras' theorem on each triangle

questions.explanation: Splitting the quadrilateral into triangles $ABC$ and $ACD$ along diagonal $AC$, you can use $\frac{1}{2}ab\sin C$ for each triangle and add the areas.
